text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Draft law makes it necessary for officials to declare their assets, one month after they take up their position.

- President Liamine Zeroual voices his strategic choices. He made clear religious parties had no place on the political scene and that Algeria would only invite representatives of those organisations of which it is member to monitor legislative elections.
- Swiss judge says thousands of weapons destined for Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front were bought in Switzerland.
- Customs authorities give ultimatum to ease ports congestion.

- Algerian-European discord after the European Parliament made reservations about the North African country's democratic process. Main political obstacles resurface after they had been almost wiped out by the presidential election.
- University teachers say determined to pursue strike and denounce education ministry stand.
- The European Parliament resolution on the situation in Algeria echoed views of political expatriates.
